1) Telemetry carveout: they want aggregate inference telemetry. We need product to confirm what "aggregate" means operationally and whether we can offer a per-customer opt-out or per-route opt-in at runtime.
2) Subprocessor vetting: they highlighted an analytics vendor (third party) — security/legal will need to check SOC2 + allowed processing scope.
3) Retention window: they propose 365d; product/security should advise acceptable retention and technical path (per-customer retention config or require Dedicated/Private).

Options I see: a) fast-track a minimal security-approved carveout with strict definition and addendum, b) require dedicated capacity for full isolation, or c) negotiate a shorter retention window + deny response-body telemetry. Product: what is the estimated effort for per-customer telemetry toggles and retention policy? Security: what are the gating criteria you'd need to sign off? Thanks for the ping, Karthik. Quick assessment from Product: 

- "Aggregate telemetry" needs a concrete definition. Operationally we can provide metrics at the route/model/tenant level (latency p50/p95, token counts, error rates) without storing request/response payloads. We do not currently have a per-customer toggle for telemetry exports; that's a feature. Estimated work: ~2 sprints (3 engineers) to add per-tenant telemetry flags + per-tenant retention config surfaced in Console.

- Retention: system default 90 days for detailed telemetry; we can extend to 365 days via a config but that will increase infra cost and monitoring needs. Offering 365d for a single enterprise customer is doable as a paid add-on or as part of Dedicated.

- Subprocessors: exposing the subprocessor list is straightforward; if Celerity needs contract-level guarantees around a specific analytics provider, we either require vendor SOC2 evidence and a limited scope (no raw PII), or advise Dedicated/Private deployment.

Proposed short reply to Celerity: explain what telemetry we can provide today (aggregated metrics, no raw responses), offer a timeline for per-tenant controls (2 sprints) as a commercial/engineering priority, and request SOC2 + description from the analytics vendor. Meanwhile, Security should propose the exact guardrail language they need in the DPA so Legal can apply it.

I can draft the product-side redline for the DPA (technical exhibit) if Priyom confirms the security constraints. If Procurement needs the language by 09/24, we either (A) provide a narrowly-scoped telemetry carveout that excludes request/response and requires vendor attestations, or (B) offer Dedicated as a blocker-removal but with different procurement timeline.

Happy to jump on a 30m sync with Procurement + Security — suggest Wed 09/22 10:00am PT.

- Olga
Product Manager, Runtime Platform

Appreciate the context. Security stance and suggested redline below. High-level summary: we can approve a narrow telemetry carveout if and only if all three conditions are met. I included a suggested clause you can drop into the DPA.

Security gating conditions (must all be satisfied):
1) No raw request/response payloads may be exported or shared with Celerity; only aggregated, non-identifiable operational metrics (latency, error rates, token counts) are allowed. Aggregation must be across a minimum of N=10 requests per reporting bucket or be windowed to avoid single-request exposure.
2) Any subprocessor used for analytics must provide SOC2 Type II evidence and a signed data-processing adendum limiting access to de-identified operational metrics; Redwood must receive the evidence prior to subprocessor being permitted to process Celerity-related data.
3) Retention: telemetry retention for this carveout is capped at 180 days unless the customer commits to Dedicated capacity or signs a paid retention add-on.

Suggested DPA language (security-redline):
"Notwithstanding other provisions, Provider may generate and share aggregated operational metrics related to Service performance (e.g., request latency percentiles, request counts, error rates, and token usage) with Customer solely for the purposes of service performance monitoring and billing. Provider shall not export or disclose raw request or response content. Aggregated metrics shall be computed in a manner that prevents identification of individual requests or users (e.g., minimum aggregation thresholds or time-windowing). Any third-party subprocessor engaged to compute or host such metrics shall provide Provider with current SOC2 Type II evidence and shall be bound by a Data Processing Addendum that restricts processing to aggregated, non-identifiable metrics. Telemetry retention for Customer-specific aggregated metrics under this carveout shall not exceed 180 days unless otherwise agreed in writing as part of a Dedicated deployment or explicit retention addendum."

If Product can accept the 180d cap and the aggregation constraints (N=10 or time-windowing), Security can sign off on a narrow carveout ASAP. Legal should review the redline for phrasing.

Action items:
- Olga: confirm feasibility of N=10 aggregation/windowing and whether the per-tenant toggle + retention config can be surfaced to Console in the proposed 2-sprint timeline.
- Ben/Karthik: confirm whether Commercial is willing to offer 180d retention as default and treat 365d as a paid add-on or Dedicated requirement.
- Karthik: if Procurement wants to proceed, propose the redline above and request SOC2 + vendor description; we will sign off pending vendor attestation.

I can join the Wed 09/22 sync if needed; otherwise Legal/Contracts can produce the formal redline.

— Priyom
